title: Product of Everything Else
statement:
Given an array of integers nums, return an array out of the same length where out[i] is the product of every element of nums except nums[i].

Solve it in O(n) time without using division. The input can contain zeros, so dividing a total product would fail anyway.

examples.why: Every product that includes the 0 is 0. Only the 0's own slot skips it: 5·(-2)·3 = -30. Dividing the total by nums[i] would divide by zero here.
With two zeros, every product still contains at least one of them.

constraints: Every prefix and suffix product fits in a 32-bit signed integer
hints: out[i] is (product of everything to the left of i) × (product of everything to the right of i). Can you get those two numbers for every i quickly?
One pass from the left can record the running product before each index. A second pass from the right can do the same for the right side.
Store the left products in the output array, then walk from the right with a single running variable and multiply it in. No extra array needed.

explain.intuition:
Split "everything except i" into two parts: everything before i and everything after i. A running product from the left gives the first part for every index in one pass. A running product from the right gives the second part in another pass. Multiply them and you are done, with no division, so zeros cause no trouble.

It is the same shape as prefix sums, just with multiplication: precompute running totals once so every query is O(1).
steps: Create out of length n. Walk left to right with left = 1: set out[i] = left, then left *= nums[i].
Now out[i] holds the product of everything before i.
Walk right to left with right = 1: set out[i] *= right, then right *= nums[i].
pitfalls: Updating the running product before writing it, which includes nums[i] in its own answer.
Dividing the total by nums[i]: breaks on any zero, and the problem forbids it.
Starting the running products at 0 instead of 1.

solutions.title: Multiply the others directly
solutions.idea: For each index, multiply every other element. Correct but quadratic.

solutions.title: Left and right product arrays
solutions.idea: left[i] is the product before i, right[i] the product after i. The answer is their product.

solutions.title: Two passes, one running variable
solutions.idea: Write the left products into the output, then sweep from the right with a single running product.

followups: If division were allowed, how would you handle zeros correctly? Count them first.
Return the sum of everything except nums[i] instead. Which part of the idea carries over?
